introduction: The study aimed to make a preliminary assessment of depression rates and physical activity levels, and the relationship between them, among Polish and Portuguese students in the further year of the COVID-19 pandemic. The authors note that restrictions on exercise have largely led to a decline in daily physical activity.
methodology: An online cross-sectional survey of students from Poland and Portugal, conducted in October 2022 with a Google form shared through e-learning platforms and Facebook private groups. The analysed sample was 398 students (229 from Poland, 169 from Portugal), aged 17 to 26. Depression was measured with the Beck Depression Inventory and physical activity with an abbreviated International Physical Activity Questionnaire (IPAQ). Analyses used Mann–Whitney, chi-square, Spearman’s rank correlation and Kruskal–Wallis tests in Statistica v. 13.
results: Moderate depression affected 20–35% of respondents, and depression was generally lower among men. There were no differences between countries in the distribution of depression classifications. Portuguese women showed a different activity profile, with fewer in the low-activity group (16% vs. 34%). In both countries, more frequent walking had the strongest effect on reducing depression (Poland rS = −0.42; Portugal rS = −0.28).
discussion: The authors report that depression severity tended to decrease with more physical activity, and that a subgroup analysis showed physical activity at a certain intensity could reduce students’ depressiveness. They describe the prevalence of depression among these students as alarming and conclude that further research on physical activity and mental health is needed to adjust the optimal level of activity.
limitations: The authors state that the cross-sectional nature of the study does not provide robust and causal evidence, that the small sample and preliminary findings are limitations, and that self-report questionnaires may bias responses. They also note that social media may distort the data and affect the representativeness of the sample. They propose future studies with a larger sample and more objective methods to assess the parameters studied.

introduction.q: The aim of the study was to make a preliminary assessment of depression rates and levels of physical activity as well as relationship between physical activity and depression among Polish and Portuguese students in the further year of the COVID-19 pandemic.
Restrictions on exercise, and bans on gyms, swimming pools, and health clubs have largely led to a decline in daily physical activity

methodology.q: students from Poland and Portugal participated in an online cross-sectional survey

The researchers distributed the survey by providing links to a Google form that asked students to participate in the survey on online e-learning platforms and on social media (Facebook) in private groups.
A total of 398 questionnaires were correctly completed and this group was analyzed.
The study included 229 questionnaires from Poland and 169 from Portugal.
The students polled ranged in age from 17 to 26 years.
The level of depression was assessed using the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) in Polish and in Portuguese.
The level of physical activity was assessed using an abbreviated version of the International Physical Activity Questionnaire (IPAQ) in Polish and Portuguese
The Mann–Whitney test was used to determine the significance of differences in depression severity (BDI) and physical activity level (IPAQ) between groups of Portuguese and Polish students
the chi-square test of independence was used to determine differences in the percentage distribution of depression level classification and activity level
Spearman’s rank correlation coefficient was used to calculate correlations between depression severity and physical activity.
The Kruskal–Wallis test was used to determine the significance of differences in depression severity (BDI) versus activity level classification.
For statistical analysis, Statistica v. 13 software was used

results.q: Moderate depression affected 20–35% of the respondents, while more severe depressive states occurred sporadically.

results.q: In both countries, more frequent walking had the strongest effect on reducing BDI (in Poland, rS = −0.42; in Portugal, rS = −0.28).
In Portuguese women, there was no statistically significant correlation between activity and depression

discussion.q: Our study also shows a tendency for depression severity to decrease with increased physical activity.
In our study, a subgroup analysis showed that physical activity at a certain intensity could reduce students’ depressiveness.

Further research should be conducted on the impact of physical activity on mental health in different populations, with the aim of adjusting the optimal level of physical activity for the alleviation of negative mental symptoms.

it was alarming that, in the second year of the pandemic, after most sanitary restrictions had been lifted and the vaccine COVID-19 had been released for general use, 20-35% of respondents were still affected by moderate depression.

limitations.q: First, the cross-sectional nature of the study does not provide robust and causal evidence for the observed associations.
The second limitation was the small sample group and preliminary findings.
Social media particularly attracts stressed individuals looking for support, which may distort the data and affect the representativeness of the sample.
All data were collected using self-report questionnaires, which may bias responses
Future studies should target a larger sample and use more objective methods to assess the parameters studied.

abstract_claims.q: Overall, 20–35% of respondents suffered from moderate depression, with a lower proportion among men.
There were no differences in the percentage distribution of depression classification between Polish and Portuguese students.
A decrease in the severity of depression was observed with increasing physical activity.
In both countries, walking more often had the strongest effect on reducing depression scores.
The continued and alarming prevalence of depressive disorders among university students in the year after the pandemic began had a significant impact on this population

further research on the impact of physical activity on mental health in different populations should be conducted to adjust the optimal level of physical activity for alleviating negative psychiatric symptoms.

caveats.q: Although our own study found that the majority of students were not depressed
although there are no differences between countries on the overall measure
caveats.loc: 3.3. Comparison of Activities by Student Gender

caveats.q: in Polish women the only statistically significant (p = 0.0155 ...) but very weak correlation (rS = −0.21) was between walking intensity and depression
The negative sign of the correlation means that more walking had a positive effect on the psyche, resulting in a minimal reduction in the severity of depression.
In general, however, a weak trend toward a decrease in depression severity with increasing activity can be seen in the Polish group.
When the IPAQ is split into groups, some information is lost, and it is therefore more difficult to obtain a statistically significant relationship.

because the differences in depression severity between groups with varying levels of physical activity were not statistically significant, the preceding observation should be regarded as a hypothesis for further research rather than a definitive conclusion.
The p-value was less than 0.1 only for male students from Poland, indicating a difference close to statistical significance.
The second limitation was the small sample group and preliminary findings.
the cross-sectional nature of the study does not provide robust and causal evidence for the observed associations
The study was also conducted in an online survey format and the identity of those who responded is not known
Social media particularly attracts stressed individuals looking for support, which may distort the data and affect the representativeness of the sample.
All data were collected using self-report questionnaires, which may bias responses
Despite these limitations, the current study has a number of strengths
However, there is no definitive consensus in the literature on the optimal level of physical activity to alleviate negative psychiatric symptoms
Pilot studies have shown that there are not many statistically significant differences in depression and physical activity levels between students in Poland and Portugal.
